questions.q: Why does a data pill sometimes resolve to null even though the flow logic looks correct?
options: The referenced record or field no longer existed in the expected state when that step actually ran
Null values are always a Flow Designer platform bug
Data pills cannot resolve to null under any circumstance
The flow was deleted before it finished running
questions.explain: A record deleted or changed between the trigger and a later step is a common, real cause of a null pill.

questions.q: What happens at runtime when a required action input was left unmapped?
options: Flow Designer always blocks saving the flow, so this can never reach runtime
The step fails outright with an error naming the specific missing input
The step silently skips itself with no indication anything happened
The entire instance stops processing all flows
questions.explain: The execution log names the exact missing required input, making this an easy failure to pinpoint.

questions.q: Why can a data type mismatch in an If/Else condition be hard to spot?
options: It always crashes the flow with a loud error message
It only happens when Flow Designer itself is down
It can't actually affect which branch a condition takes
It evaluates with no error at all, just sending the flow down the unexpected branch
questions.explain: Comparing a number to a string, for example, silently changes the result without throwing any error.

questions.q: A flow is stuck at an Approval action and never progresses. What's a likely real cause?
options: The approval was routed to the wrong person or an empty group, so no one was actually notified
ServiceNow has a platform-wide limit on how many approvals can exist
Approval actions cannot ever pause a flow
The flow author forgot to include an Approval action at all
questions.explain: The flow is working as designed; it's just waiting on a response that will never arrive.

questions.q: When an IntegrationHub REST step fails, what should you check first in the execution log?
options: Whether the flow's trigger condition itself was configured correctly
Whether the flow has too many actions overall
The actual error on that step — pointing to an expired credential alias or an unreachable external system
Whether the user who built the flow still has an active account
questions.explain: The REST step's own error in the log almost always points directly to the credential alias or the external system, not the flow's design.
